Apple___Apple_scab.chemical_control: Apply a protectant fungicide such as captan or a sterol-inhibiting fungicide at green tip and through primary scab season, following local label rates.
Apple___Apple_scab.organic_control: Use sulfur or potassium bicarbonate sprays during wet weather. Rake and destroy fallen leaves to reduce overwintering inoculum.
Apple___Apple_scab.preventative_measures: Prune for airflow, choose scab-resistant cultivars, and avoid overhead irrigation during leaf wetness periods.

Apple___healthy.organic_control: Maintain orchard sanitation and beneficial insect habitat.
Apple___healthy.preventative_measures: Continue regular scouting, balanced nutrition, and pruning to keep canopy airflow high.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.chemical_control: Apply sulfur or a registered DMI/QoI fungicide at the first sign of white mycelium, rotating modes of action.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.organic_control: Use potassium bicarbonate or wettable sulfur. Remove and destroy heavily infected shoots.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.preventative_measures: Prune for sunlight and airflow, avoid excess nitrogen, and do not wet foliage late in the day.

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.organic_control: Keep trees well mulched and monitor for early powdery growth on young leaves.
Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.preventative_measures: Maintain open canopy, irrigate at the base, and inspect weekly during humid weather.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.chemical_control: If pustules are spreading on susceptible hybrids, apply a foliar fungicide (strobilurin or triazole) according to growth stage and label.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.organic_control: Remove heavily infected volunteer plants. Use compost teas only as a supplement to scouting, not as a standalone cure.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.preventative_measures: Plant rust-tolerant hybrids, rotate crops, and avoid late planting in rust-prone regions.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.organic_control: Preserve beneficial insects and avoid unnecessary sprays.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.preventative_measures: Use certified seed, balanced fertility, and routine scouting for rust pustules after tasseling.

Grape___Black_rot.chemical_control: Apply protectant fungicides (mancozeb, captan, or strobilurins) from early shoot growth through bunch close, especially before rain.
Grape___Black_rot.organic_control: Remove mummified berries and infected leaves. Copper and sulfur programs can reduce spread in organic vineyards.
Grape___Black_rot.preventative_measures: Improve canopy airflow, sanitize the trellis of last season's mummies, and avoid prolonged leaf wetness.

Grape___healthy.organic_control: Keep vineyard floor clean of mummies and prunings.
Grape___healthy.preventative_measures: Continue canopy management, drip irrigation, and pre-rain scouting during bloom.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.chemical_control: Apply copper during dormancy and early season; use registered antibiotic or copper programs only where labeled and resistance is managed.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.organic_control: Remove and destroy infected fruit and leaves. Copper sprays in dormancy plus strict sanitation.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.preventative_measures: Plant less susceptible cultivars, avoid overhead irrigation, and disinfect pruning tools between trees.

Peach___healthy.organic_control: Maintain orchard sanitation and copper-free unless local extension advises a dormant spray.
Peach___healthy.preventative_measures: Scout fruit and leaves after storms; keep nitrogen moderate to avoid succulent tissue.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.chemical_control: Use copper plus mancozeb where labeled, and rotate with other registered bactericides. Avoid antibiotics unless locally recommended.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.organic_control: Remove severely spotted leaves, apply copper carefully, and use composted mulch to reduce splash.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.preventative_measures: Start with certified disease-free transplants, avoid working plants when wet, and rotate away from solanaceous crops.

Pepper,_bell___healthy.organic_control: Keep beds weed-free and inspect undersides of leaves weekly.
Pepper,_bell___healthy.preventative_measures: Drip irrigate, space plants for airflow, and sanitize trays and stakes.

Potato___Early_blight.chemical_control: Apply chlorothalonil, mancozeb, or a registered strobilurin/DMI program on a protectant schedule once lesions appear.
Potato___Early_blight.organic_control: Remove lower infected leaves, use copper or Bacillus-based biofungicides, and increase potassium if deficient.
Potato___Early_blight.preventative_measures: Rotate out of potatoes/tomatoes for 2–3 years, hill properly, and avoid overhead irrigation late in the day.

Potato___Late_blight.chemical_control: Apply a late-blight specific fungicide (e.g., cyazofamid, mandipropamid, or local equivalent) immediately; protectant-only programs are often insufficient.
Potato___Late_blight.organic_control: Destroy infected plants and volunteers. Copper can slow spread but will not eradicate an active outbreak.
Potato___Late_blight.preventative_measures: Use certified seed tubers, destroy cull piles, and monitor weather-based blight forecasts daily.

Potato___healthy.organic_control: Keep foliage dry and remove volunteer potatoes.
Potato___healthy.preventative_measures: Scout twice weekly in cool, wet weather and maintain hilling to protect tubers.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.chemical_control: Rotate sulfur, potassium bicarbonate, and registered DMI/QoI fungicides at the first sign of white colonies.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.organic_control: Apply sulfur, potassium bicarbonate, or milk-based sprays early. Remove heavily infected leaves.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.preventative_measures: Choose tolerant varieties, avoid dense planting, and water at soil level.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.chemical_control: Apply a labeled foliar fungicide during wet periods if lesions expand from older leaves into the canopy.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.organic_control: Remove old infected leaves after harvest. Use wide spacing and organic mulch to reduce splash.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.preventative_measures: Renew plantings on schedule, avoid overhead irrigation, and do not over-fertilize with nitrogen.

Strawberry___healthy.organic_control: Keep beds weeded and remove dead leaves during renovation.
Strawberry___healthy.preventative_measures: Maintain drip irrigation and inspect after prolonged rain.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.chemical_control: Apply copper-based bactericides with mancozeb where labeled; discontinue if phytotoxicity appears.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.organic_control: Remove infected foliage, use copper judiciously, and mulch to limit soil splash.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.preventative_measures: Use pathogen-free seed/transplants, avoid working wet plants, and rotate away from tomatoes and peppers.

Tomato___Early_blight.chemical_control: Begin a protectant fungicide program (chlorothalonil, mancozeb, or equivalent) at first target-like lesions on lower leaves.
Tomato___Early_blight.organic_control: Strip lower affected leaves, mulch heavily, and use copper or biofungicides as a supplement.
Tomato___Early_blight.preventative_measures: Stake/prune for airflow, water at the base, and rotate out of solanaceous crops.

Tomato___Late_blight.chemical_control: Treat immediately with a late-blight specific fungicide; protectants alone rarely stop an active epidemic.
Tomato___Late_blight.organic_control: Remove and destroy infected plants (do not compost). Copper may slow but not stop rapid outbreaks.
Tomato___Late_blight.preventative_measures: Avoid overhead watering, increase spacing, and respond to blight warnings the same day.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.chemical_control: In protected culture, apply a labeled fungicide and rotate FRAC groups. Improve greenhouse climate control first.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.organic_control: Lower humidity, increase ventilation, and remove infected lower leaves.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.preventative_measures: Keep night humidity down, avoid leaf wetness, and space plants for airflow.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.chemical_control: Apply protectant fungicides to new growth after removing heavily spotted lower leaves.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.organic_control: Mulch to stop soil splash, prune lower canopy, and use copper or biofungicides early.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.preventative_measures: Stake plants, drip irrigate, and disinfect cages and stakes between seasons.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.chemical_control: Use a selective miticide (not a broad-spectrum insecticide that kills predators). Repeat per label if populations rebound.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.organic_control: Spray insecticidal soap or horticultural oil on leaf undersides. Release predatory mites where available.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.preventative_measures: Avoid dusty, drought-stressed plants; hose undersides of leaves; do not overuse pyrethroids.

Tomato___Target_Spot.chemical_control: Apply a labeled foliar fungicide at the first concentric lesions and continue through humid weather.
Tomato___Target_Spot.organic_control: Remove infected leaves and fruit. Improve airflow and use copper or biofungicides early.
Tomato___Target_Spot.preventative_measures: Mulch, stake, and avoid wetting fruit and foliage. Rotate away from tomatoes.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.chemical_control: Chemicals do not cure the virus. Control whitefly vectors with labeled insecticides or oils as part of an IPM program.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.organic_control: Rogue infected plants immediately. Use reflective mulch, insect-proof netting, and insecticidal soap on whiteflies.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.preventative_measures: Plant resistant cultivars, manage weeds that host whiteflies, and use virus-free transplants.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.chemical_control: No chemical cure. Disinfect tools with 0.5% sodium hypochlorite or equivalent between plants.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.organic_control: Remove and destroy infected plants. Wash hands after handling tobacco or infected tissue.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.preventative_measures: Use certified seed, avoid smoking near plants, and do not reuse contaminated strings or clips.

Tomato___healthy.organic_control: Support beneficial insects and keep foliage dry.
Tomato___healthy.preventative_measures: Continue staking, base watering, and weekly scouting of lower leaves.

ants.chemical_control: Use bait stations rather than broadcast sprays so worker ants carry product to the colony.
ants.organic_control: Remove honeydew sources (aphids), use diatomaceous earth on trails, and keep fruit off the soil.
ants.preventative_measures: Seal irrigation leaks, keep the field weed-free, and manage sap-feeding insects that attract ants.

beetle.chemical_control: Apply a labeled foliar insecticide if defoliation exceeds local thresholds; time sprays for adult activity.
beetle.organic_control: Hand-pick adults, use row covers on seedlings, and apply neem or spinosad where permitted.
beetle.preventative_measures: Rotate crops, destroy crop residue, and use trap crops at field edges.

catterpillar.chemical_control: Use a labeled insecticide targeting Lepidoptera larvae; Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) is effective on young caterpillars.
catterpillar.organic_control: Apply Bt or spinosad, hand-pick larvae, and encourage parasitoid wasps.
catterpillar.preventative_measures: Scout terminals twice weekly, destroy egg masses, and avoid spraying broad-spectrum products that kill predators.

earwig.chemical_control: Apply a labeled insecticide as a barrier at the base of plants only if fruit feeding is confirmed.
earwig.organic_control: Trap with oil-filled containers, reduce mulch against stems, and keep harvest debris cleaned up.
earwig.preventative_measures: Reduce excessive moisture and hiding places near fruiting plants.

grasshopper.chemical_control: Treat nymphs at field margins with a labeled insecticide before they move into the crop.
grasshopper.organic_control: Use nosema/biopesticides where available, till egg-laying sites, and maintain grassy trap strips that can be treated.
grasshopper.preventative_measures: Scout borders early in the season and keep weeds down adjacent to the field.

moth.chemical_control: Target larvae, not flying adults. Use pheromone disruption or labeled larvicides when catches exceed thresholds.
moth.organic_control: Use pheromone traps, Bt on young larvae, and night lighting only if it does not attract more pests.
moth.preventative_measures: Destroy infested fruit, time plantings to avoid peak flights, and keep orchard sanitation high.

slug.chemical_control: Apply iron phosphate or metaldehyde baits (where legal) in the evening along plant rows.
slug.organic_control: Use iron phosphate baits, beer traps, and copper tape on raised beds. Reduce irrigation at night.
slug.preventative_measures: Clear weeds and boards, improve drainage, and harvest ripe fruit promptly.

snail.chemical_control: Use labeled molluscicide baits in damp weather when snails are active.
snail.organic_control: Hand-collect at dusk, apply iron phosphate baits, and use copper barriers.
snail.preventative_measures: Remove daytime hiding places and avoid over-mulching against stems.

wasp.chemical_control: Do not spray the crop routinely. Treat nests only with a labeled product if they threaten workers.
wasp.organic_control: Protect ripening fruit with bags or nets; wasps are often beneficial predators of caterpillars.
wasp.preventative_measures: Harvest ripe fruit daily and remove fallen fruit that attracts foraging wasps.

weevil.chemical_control: Apply a labeled insecticide at the first sign of adult feeding or egg-laying, following crop-specific timing.
weevil.organic_control: Use pheromone traps, destroy infested fruit/tubers, and apply entomopathogenic nematodes where recommended.
weevil.preventative_measures: Rotate crops, destroy residue, and avoid planting next to last season's infested fields.

aphids.chemical_control: Use a selective aphicide or insecticidal soap; avoid unnecessary pyrethroids that flare outbreaks.
aphids.organic_control: Blast with water, apply insecticidal soap or neem, and conserve lady beetles and lacewings.
aphids.preventative_measures: Scout new growth twice weekly, control ants, and avoid excess nitrogen.

Thrips.chemical_control: Apply a labeled thrips material to flowers and growing tips; rotate modes of action because resistance is common.
Thrips.organic_control: Use blue sticky traps, predatory mites, and spinosad where permitted. Remove heavily scarred blooms.
Thrips.preventative_measures: Keep weeds down, use fine-mesh netting on seedlings, and avoid bringing infested transplants into clean houses.

corn borer.chemical_control: Time foliar insecticides or Bt to egg hatch before larvae bore into stalks. Consider Bt hybrids where appropriate.
corn borer.organic_control: Use Bt sprays on young larvae, shred stalks after harvest, and encourage parasitoids.
corn borer.preventative_measures: Rotate crops, destroy infested stalks, and monitor with pheromone traps.

army worm.chemical_control: Treat larvae while they are small with a labeled insecticide or Bt; large larvae are much harder to kill.
army worm.organic_control: Apply Bt or spinosad early, plow to disrupt pupae, and use trap crops at borders.
army worm.preventative_measures: Scout leaf whorls and field edges after storms and keep grassy weeds mowed.

peach borer.chemical_control: Apply a trunk-directed insecticide at the base during adult flight as recommended by local degree-day models.
peach borer.organic_control: Use mating disruption, keep trunks weed-free, and mechanically remove gummosis with larvae when found.
peach borer.preventative_measures: Avoid trunk wounds, paint or wrap young trunks, and monitor with pheromone traps.

flea beetle.chemical_control: Treat seedlings if shot-hole damage exceeds local thresholds; later-stage plants often tolerate feeding.
flea beetle.organic_control: Use row covers until flowering, apply kaolin or spinosad, and keep weeds that host beetles under control.
flea beetle.preventative_measures: Delay planting slightly if possible, use trap crops, and avoid planting next to last year's brassica or solanaceous residue.

Viteus vitifoliae.chemical_control: On own-rooted vines, soil insecticides are rarely fully effective; follow local phylloxera recommendations.
Viteus vitifoliae.organic_control: There is no reliable organic knockdown. Focus on vine vigor and rootstock strategy.
Viteus vitifoliae.preventative_measures: Plant on resistant rootstocks, prevent soil movement on equipment, and do not plant own-rooted vines in infested sites.

longlegged spider mite.chemical_control: Use a selective miticide; confirm species because some products are weak on this mite.
longlegged spider mite.organic_control: Apply horticultural oil or soap to undersides of leaves and release predatory mites.
longlegged spider mite.preventative_measures: Avoid dusty conditions and broad-spectrum insecticides that kill mite predators.

Scirtothrips dorsalis Hood.chemical_control: Apply a labeled thrips insecticide to new flush; rotate IRAC groups.
Scirtothrips dorsalis Hood.organic_control: Use spinosad, reflective mulch, and predatory mites. Remove infested flush if practical.
Scirtothrips dorsalis Hood.preventative_measures: Inspect incoming plants, keep weeds down, and use fine-mesh screens in nurseries.

Prodenia litura.chemical_control: Treat young larvae with a labeled insecticide or Bt; spray in the evening when larvae feed.
Prodenia litura.organic_control: Hand-pick, use NPV/Bt products where available, and install pheromone traps.
Prodenia litura.preventative_measures: Scout undersides of leaves for egg masses and destroy crop residue after harvest.
